basis.governing_question: How can Metalúrgica Norte cut conversion cost across its six plants in Portugal and Spain and put the improvements in place in every plant?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish where conversion cost per part arises in each plant and size the improvements that would reduce it.

gate.label: Initiative go/no-go
gate.decision: Go or no-go on the sized improvements, and which plant pilots them first?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Carry out the approved improvements at a pilot plant, roll them out to the other plants, and track savings.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the final results and the running improvements in all six plants?

workstreams.name: Floor diagnosis, two plants
workstreams.answers: Where does conversion cost per part sit in the first two plants diagnosed, and what drives it?
activities: Observe production lines and map conversion losses
Build cost-per-part baselines from operational data
Interview the people who run the lines on loss causes

workstreams.name: Remaining plants baseline
workstreams.answers: Where does conversion cost per part sit in the third diagnosed plant and the three plants covered from data?
activities: Diagnose the third plant on the floor in a second round
Extend the baseline to the other three plants from data
Test extended baselines with the people who run each plant

workstreams.name: Improvement sizing by plant
workstreams.answers: Which improvements, sized per plant, cut conversion cost per part measurably, and which plant pilots first?
activities: Build the improvement list from loss and cost findings
Size each improvement per plant in conversion cost per part
Compare the plants as candidates to pilot first

workstreams.name: Pilot plant improvements
workstreams.answers: Do the approved improvements show savings in the cost data at the pilot plant?
activities: Prepare the pilot plant's changes for the readiness review
Make the approved changes on the lines with plant teams
Measure savings in the cost data against the baseline

workstreams.name: Cost per part tracking
workstreams.answers: What conversion cost per part does each plant show against its baseline once the improvements run?
activities: Set up the tracker on each plant's cost-per-part baseline
Report cost per part by plant as each wave goes live
Test each plant's result against the success criteria

workstreams.name: Plant rollout, wave 1
workstreams.answers: How are the improvements put in place in the first wave of plants so they run there?
activities: Adapt the pilot's changes to each plant in the wave
Make the changes in the wave's plants with their teams
Train plant teams to run the changes themselves

workstreams.name: Plant rollout, wave 2
workstreams.answers: How are the improvements put in place in the remaining plants so they run in all six?
activities: Adjust the rollout to what the first wave showed
Make the changes in the remaining plants with their teams
Train plant teams to run the changes themselves

deliverables.name: Cost-per-part baseline and loss map, first two plants
Go/no-go pack: baselines, sizing and pilot plant options
Pilot plant change plan and readiness pack
Go-live record for pilot plant changes
Pilot plant savings against the cost baseline
Cost-per-part tracker on each plant's baseline
Cost-per-part report by plant after wave 1
Final readout pack: cost per part and rollout status
Go-live and team training record, wave 1 plants
Go-live and team training record, remaining plants

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start the diagnostic and secure data access
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Will each plant give the team cost data and floor access from week 1?
agenda: Present the two phases and the diagnostic work plan
Align on the cost data the baselines need from each plant
Confirm plant access and contacts for the first weeks

events.label: Workshop 1: baselines
events.purpose: Review baselines and shortlist pilot plants
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Which plants should the go/no-go pack carry as pilot options?
agenda: Present the cost-per-part baselines for all six plants
Review the loss map from the first two plants
Decide which plants go forward as pilot options in the pack

events.label: Initiative go/no-go
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Go or no-go on the sized improvements, and which plant pilots them first?
agenda: Present the sized improvement list by plant
Review the go/no-go pack and the pilot plant options
Decide on going ahead and which plant pilots first

events.label: Workshop 2: pilot readiness
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Go or no-go on taking the pilot plant changes live as planned?
agenda: Present the pilot plant change plan and readiness pack
Review readiness of the pilot plant before go-live
Decide on go-live of the pilot plant changes

events.label: Check-in: pilot results
events.purpose: Review pilot go-live, savings and tracker
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Confirm the pilot plant changes to roll out in wave 1?
agenda: Present the pilot go-live record and savings against baseline
Review the cost-per-part tracker on each plant's baseline
Confirm the pilot changes to roll out in wave 1

events.label: Workshop 3: wave 1 go-live
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Go or no-go on wave 2 in the remaining plants, using the wave 1 approach?
agenda: Present the wave 1 go-live and team training record
Discuss the cost-per-part results the final readout will report
Decide on starting wave 2 in the remaining plants

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Approve final results and running changes
attendees: Plant Directors of the six plants
events.decision: Approve the final results and the running improvements in all six plants?
agenda: Present the final readout pack on cost per part and rollout status
Review the wave 1 cost report and the wave 2 go-live record
Decide on approving the results and running improvements

architect_notes: The brief gives no engagement length, so the 25 to 29 weeks are an estimate from the work sizing, not a stated length.
Implementation takes the middle of a 16 to 24 week estimate; a 12-week pilot plant and 6-week waves would push it to the top.
Diagnostic assumes three representative plants are diagnosed on the floor and the other three extended from data; which plants is open.
No Measurement phase: results tracking runs inside Implementation, so post-launch tracking beyond the last wave needs the partner's decision.

sub_questions.question: Where does conversion cost per part sit in each plant today, and what drives it?
Which improvements, sized per plant, cut conversion cost per part by a measurable amount in every plant?
Do the approved improvements show savings in the cost data at the pilot plant?
How are the improvements put in place in the other plants so they are running in all six plants?
What conversion cost per part does each plant show against its baseline once the improvements run?

drivers.evidence: six plants in Portugal and Spain

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Site diagnosed on the floor (cost baseline, line observation, loss analysis)

phases.why: Three plants diagnosed two at a time, the other three extended from data; above typical 3-6 weeks because three plants need two rounds.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: Pilot site: changes made and savings shown in the cost data
Rollout wave of up to 3 sites

phases.why: Pilot plant, then two rollout waves for the other five plants in sequence; above the typical 8-16 weeks because the work adds up.

sizing.levers: Running the two rollout waves side by side would cut the most; diagnosing two plants instead of three saves about two weeks.
